title: roleblend-probe-archives
content:
Purpose:
A personal scratchpad for experiments that try to 1) blend multiple persona/role primings in a single multi-turn session, 2) make few-shot anchors graduated (soft-to-hard anchoring), and 3) measure failure modes when prompts compete for token budget. Goal is a small, reproducible set of templates and counterexamples to feed into the prompt library and unit tests.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Keep templates short; long system priming eats KV cache and destroys latency on long contexts.
- Test with temperature schedule: 0.0 for anchors, 0.2 for scaffolding, 0.6 for final answer.
- Measure per-shot latency and per-token cost; log token counts.

Experiment 1: Roleblend base template (hybrid persona)
- Intent: combine domain-expert persona with empathic assistant.
- Template (minimal):
  System: You are an assistant that answers as both a domain expert (concise, numbered steps) and as an empathic coach (tone: supportive). At the end, append a 1-sentence summary for a non-technical reader.
  User: "Describe how to debug a cache miss in our inference runtime for a slow tail latency symptom."

Few-shot anchors (graduated):
- Anchor A (soft): Short example, 1 line, hinting style.
  Q: Why might requests stall?
  A: Network retries or kernel stalls; check NIC and driver logs. (tone: fact + calm)
- Anchor B (hard): Full structured example, numbered steps.
  Q: How to confirm KV cache eviction?
  A: 1) Reproduce with controlled seq len; 2) inspect runtime metrics; 3) enable debug flags and collect traces. Summary: check eviction counters.

Recorded failure cases (observed):
- Conflict: when Anchor A contradicts Anchor B on recommended command names, model mixes commands -> hallucination.
- Tone bleed: empathic phrasing appears inside code snippet lines -> test harness expects plain code.
- Token budget: long persona + 2 hard anchors pushes context beyond preferred window for cheap 7B variant -> observable cost spike.

Hypotheses / causes:
- Model treats 'append a 1-sentence summary' as part of same numbered list; need explicit separator token like '---' or 'SUMMARY:'
- Hard anchors that include command names become stronger priors and override system instructions in some runs; possibly due to recency bias when anchors are later in context.

Mitigations to try (next runs):
- Move anchors earlier and include explicit instruction: 'Ignore examples for command names, only borrow style.'
- Insert '###' separator before final answer request to prevent list merging.
- Try control token: <NO-TONE> marker before code blocks.

Experiment 2: Few-shot selection by latency-aware heuristics
- Idea: use a cheap lexical similarity filter to select 1-2 anchors rather than including full canned set.
- Selection pipeline notes: precompute embedding centroid of last 128 tokens of user message; pick closest example(s) from < curated pool >.

Quick example pair (for library):
- Example 1:
  Q: "How to minimize per-token cost for chat with many short turns?"
  A: "1) Increase batching window for short-turn bursts; 2) enable prefix caching for stable prompts; 3) set predictable route to dedicated capacity. TL;DR: batch + cache."
- Example 2:
  Q: "Summarize rollout strategy for a minor model update."
  A: "Start with canary (1%), measure regressions on eval set, incrementally increase with automated rollback on quality drop."

Metrics to log:
- success_rate_on_eval_prompts (binary pass/fail per rubric)
- median_latency_ms_at_95th
- token_cost_per_response
- hallucination_count (manual annotations for now)

Quick checklist before adding template to prompt-library:
- [ ] minimal system text (< 120 tokens)
- [ ] 1-2 anchors only, prefer soft anchor first
- [ ] explicit separators for summary/code blocks
- [ ] test across 3 model variants: small/medium/large
- [ ] record token counts and latency; attach sample outputs

Open questions / TODOs:
- Does moving anchors earlier always improve fidelity, or is there a sweet spot? Try offset experiments.
- Can we auto-generate anchor variants that differ only in tone to measure tone bleed?
- Add unit test that checks for inadvertent inclusion of persona tokens inside code fences.

Scratch outputs (raw) from 2026-02-14 run (for quick debugging):
- Prompt sent (truncated): System+AnchorA+AnchorB+User -> 842 tokens
- Output (summary): ended up embedding 'Step 0:' inside code block, failure-> pattern match triggered.

Notes for prompt-librarian entry: recommended filename: roleblend-hybrid-1; tags: roleblend, graduated-anchors, latency-aware-selection. Include sample anchors and a short rubric for passing (no command hallucinations, summary present, tone balanced).

References/links:
- PR with selection filter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lab/pull/78
- Ticket: PROJ-4321 (experiment tracking for roleblend)

End notes: keep iterative, prefer shorter anchors, log everything. This doc is ephemeral; once templated and unit-tested, move canonical copy to confluence and mark final.
